es: Escribir un párrafo persuasivo con una afirmación enfática (so/such), una pregunta retórica, un tricolon, una objeción admitida y una llamada a la acción concreta.

teaching.en: Our city has such heavy traffic that a short commute can take an hour, and few residents believe that the situation is sustainable.
teaching.es: Nuestra ciudad tiene un tráfico tan pesado que un trayecto corto puede durar una hora, y pocos residentes creen que la situación sea sostenible.
teaching.explanationEs: Such + adjetivo + nombre incontable (heavy traffic) + that; sustainable = que puede mantenerse.
segments: Our city has such heavy traffic that a short commute can take
an hour, and few residents believe that the situation is sustainable.
teaching.audioText: Our city has such heavy traffic that a short commute can take an hour, and few residents believe that the situation is sustainable.

teaching.en: A bicycle is so cheap and so easy to maintain that almost everyone in the community can use one.
teaching.es: Una bicicleta es tan barata y tan fácil de mantener que casi todos los miembros de la comunidad pueden usar una.
teaching.explanationEs: So + adjetivo solo + that: tan… que.
segments: A bicycle is so cheap and so easy to maintain
that almost everyone in the community can use one.
teaching.audioText: A bicycle is so cheap and so easy to maintain that almost everyone in the community can use one.

teaching.en: Why should our community go on accepting so much pollution every single day when a practical alternative already exists?
teaching.es: ¿Por qué debería nuestra comunidad seguir aceptando tanta contaminación cada día cuando ya existe una alternativa práctica?
teaching.explanationEs: Pregunta retórica con Why should…?: no espera respuesta, el público concluye solo.
segments: Why should our community go on accepting so much pollution
every single day when a practical alternative already exists?
teaching.audioText: Why should our community go on accepting so much pollution every single day when a practical alternative already exists?

teaching.en: Bikes are cheap, quick and clean, and the tangible benefit for families is more money, more time and cleaner streets.
teaching.es: Las bicis son baratas, rápidas y limpias, y la ventaja concreta para las familias es más dinero, más tiempo y calles más limpias.
teaching.explanationEs: Tricolon: tres partes con la misma forma; tangible = concreto, medible.
segments: Bikes are cheap, quick and clean, and the tangible benefit
for families is more money, more time and cleaner streets.
teaching.audioText: Bikes are cheap, quick and clean, and the tangible benefit for families is more money, more time and cleaner streets.

teaching.en: The council's new initiative aims to cut down on car journeys, so we must convince it to build a bicycle station near the school.
teaching.es: La nueva iniciativa del ayuntamiento pretende reducir los viajes en coche, así que debemos convencerlo de que construya una estación de bicicletas cerca del colegio.
teaching.explanationEs: Cut down on + nombre: reducir; convince someone to + verbo: convencer de que haga algo.
segments: The council's new initiative aims to cut down on car journeys, so
we must convince it to build a bicycle station near the school.
teaching.audioText: The council's new initiative aims to cut down on car journeys, so we must convince it to build a bicycle station near the school.

teaching.en: There is so much pollution that the community cannot ignore it, and so many cars that even short journeys feel like a waste of time.
teaching.es: Hay tanta contaminación que la comunidad no puede ignorarla, y tantos coches que hasta los trayectos cortos parecen una pérdida de tiempo.
teaching.explanationEs: So much + nombre incontable; so many + nombre plural.
segments: There is so much pollution that the community cannot ignore it, and so
many cars that even short journeys feel like a waste of time.
teaching.audioText: There is so much pollution that the community cannot ignore it, and so many cars that even short journeys feel like a waste of time.

prompt.es: Elige la versión enfática: «Es un tráfico tan pesado que nadie llega a tiempo.»

choices.text: It is such heavy traffic that nobody arrives on time.
It is so heavy traffic that nobody arrives on time.
It is such a heavy traffic that nobody arrives on time.

feedback.es: Traffic es incontable y va tras el adjetivo: such + adjetivo + nombre, sin a; so no admite nombre.

hint.es: Traffic es un nombre incontable: no lleva a.

origin.text: Describing the morning rush, a student wants her opening line to sound strong and to name the problem immediately, before she asks any questions.

prompt.es: Completa: «Una bicicleta es tan barata que casi todos pueden tener una.»

feedback.es: Tras la palabra que falta solo hay un adjetivo, así que se usa so.

hint.es: Después de la palabra que falta va un adjetivo solo, sin nombre.

origin.text: A bicycle is ___ cheap that almost everyone in the community can have one. It needs no fuel, no parking fee and very little repair.

prompt.es: Ordena: «¿Por qué debería nuestra comunidad aceptar la contaminación?»

answer.text: Why should our community accept pollution

feedback.es: La pregunta retórica se construye con Why should + sujeto + verbo.

hint.es: Empieza por la palabra interrogativa: Why should…

prompt.es: Elige el tricolon paralelo para hablar de las bicis.

choices.text: Bikes are safe, simply and fun.
Bikes are safe, simple and fun.
Bikes are safe, they are simple and to have fun.

feedback.es: Tres adjetivos con la misma forma dan el tricolon; las otras opciones mezclan formas.

origin.text: A leaflet for the new bicycle plan needs one closing line that lists three benefits in exactly the same pattern, so that it sounds balanced.

prompt.es: Dale énfasis con such: «Es una idea muy buena.»

answer.text: It is such a good idea.
accepted: It is such a good idea.
It is such a great idea.
That is such a good idea.
This is such a good idea.
It is such a nice idea.

feedback.es: Con a + adjetivo + nombre singular contable se usa such a: such a good idea.

origin.text: The council has approved public bicycles. In her blog, a resident writes: It is a very good idea.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada estructura con lo que exige después.

feedback.es: So acompaña a un adjetivo o a much/many; such necesita un nombre, con a si es contable singular y sin a si es incontable.

prompt.es: Escucha el párrafo y elige qué propone la oradora.

choices.text: A faster bus line to replace the old route.
A ban on cars near every school.
A plan for public bicycles to reduce delays.

feedback.es: Propone bicicletas públicas como solución a los retrasos; no pide una nueva línea de autobús ni prohíbe los coches, solo que se reduzca el tráfico.

origin.audio: Our streets are so crowded that a ten-minute trip takes forty minutes. Why should we accept such a waste of time? Public bicycles are cheap, quick and clean, and they would cut down on traffic near every school. Some people worry that nobody would use them, but the same plan has worked in many cities, and the benefit has been tangible. Let us ask the council to begin the plan.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige por qué la oradora menciona otras ciudades.

choices.text: To answer a doubt with evidence that the plan works.
To suggest that her city is falling behind.
To concede that the plan has worked only in small cities.

feedback.es: Recoge la duda de que nadie usaría las bicis y la contesta con un dato: el mismo sistema ha funcionado en muchas ciudades.

origin.audio: Our streets are so crowded that a ten-minute trip takes forty minutes. Why should we accept such a waste of time? Public bicycles are cheap, quick and clean, and they would cut down on traffic near every school. Some people worry that nobody would use them, but the same plan has worked in many cities, and the benefit has been tangible. Let us ask the council to begin the plan.

prompt.es: Completa: «El ayuntamiento espera reducir los trayectos en coche en toda la ciudad.»

feedback.es: Cut down on + nombre significa reducir: es la colocación habitual para hablar de disminuir el uso del coche.

origin.text: Since the bicycle plan began, thousands of people have changed the way they commute. The council now hopes to ___ down on car journeys across the whole city.

prompt.es: Escribe un párrafo persuasivo sobre bicicletas públicas para tu barrio.

answer.text: Our neighbourhood has such heavy traffic that a short trip to school takes forty minutes. Why should our children live with pollution every morning? Public bicycles are cheap, quick and clean, and they are so simple to use that anyone can try one. They would help students, workers and families, and they would make our streets calmer, safer and greener. Some people will say that the project is too expensive, but the tangible benefit for our health is far greater than the cost. Why should we wait another year for a better community? Let us ask the council to support this initiative and build a bicycle station near every school. Sign the petition today, and together we can change how our neighbourhood moves.
accepted: Our neighbourhood has such heavy traffic that a short trip to school takes forty minutes. Why should our children live with pollution every morning? Public bicycles are cheap, quick and clean, and they are so simple to use that anyone can try one. They would help students, workers and families, and they would make our streets calmer, safer and greener. Some people will say that the project is too expensive, but the tangible benefit for our health is far greater than the cost. Why should we wait another year for a better community? Let us ask the council to support this initiative and build a bicycle station near every school. Sign the petition today, and together we can change how our neighbourhood moves.

Our city has such a serious traffic problem that parents are afraid to walk their children to school. Why should a child live with pollution on the way to class? A public bicycle is cheap, quick and clean, and it is so easy to use that everybody can try it. Bicycles would bring us a tangible benefit: less noise, less pollution and more time with our families. Critics may say that the plan costs too much, but it would cut down on car journeys and save money for everyone in the long run. We must convince the council to build a bicycle station near the school. Please join our campaign and sign the petition this week, because our community deserves better streets.

feedback.es: Un párrafo persuasivo completo abre con énfasis, pregunta, enumera tres ventajas, admite una objeción y termina con una petición concreta.

origin.text: Convence a tu comunidad de instalar bicicletas públicas en tu barrio. Escribe en inglés (150–200 palabras): una afirmación con such o so, una pregunta retórica, un tricolon, una objeción que admites y una llamada a la acción dirigida al consejo.

prompt.es: Elige qué da a entender el texto sobre el programa de prueba.

choices.text: That the council is unhappy with the results so far.
That it may be extended because it was popular.
That it will certainly continue after next month.

feedback.es: Nueve de cada diez quisieron quedarse con la bici y el ayuntamiento revisará la prueba: se da a entender que podría ampliarse.

origin.text: Residents were offered a free bicycle trial for one week. After seven days, nine out of ten asked to keep the bike, and several said that they would never go back to the bus. The council has announced that it will review the trial next month.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Convenzamos al consejo de que construya una estación cerca del colegio.»

answer.text: Let us convince the council to build a station near the school

feedback.es: Convince + persona + to + verbo: la llamada a la acción pide algo concreto al consejo.

prompt.es: Completa: «Hay tantos coches que la calle parece un estacionamiento.»

feedback.es: So many + nombre plural contable + that expresa cantidad con énfasis.

origin.text: At eight o'clock the road outside the school is completely full. There are ___ many cars that the street looks like a car park.
